problem: VLM-based VLN policies use perspective images, so they miss routes outside the field of view. Simply swapping perspective images for equirectangular panoramas (ERPs) under the same training and inference setup gives little or no gain, and can even hurt.
motivation: A panorama exposes passages, landmarks and route alternatives in all directions, which should give a more complete basis for navigation decisions. The authors' diagnosis is that using it fully needs changes to action prediction, training supervision and visual representation. Branching points are also sparse in existing VLN data, and VLM features carry semantics but little spatial layout.
key_idea: Adapt a VLM policy to ERP input with long-horizon action prediction and confidence-guided execution, decision-centric branching-route data, and aligned PanoVGGT geometric features fused into the visual tokens.
insight: Panoramic input only pays off when supervision matches the visible route information. In the horizon ablation, ERP policies trail perspective ones at short horizons but overtake them as targets lengthen; perspective peaks at H=4 and ERP at H=18. Uncertainty-based CGE beats every fixed execution length, including one action per call (R2R-CE SR 66.6 vs 64.6). Geometry helps only with a panorama-specific encoder: PanoVGGT lifts R2R-CE SR from 66.6 to 68.6, while DA2 and DAP have mixed or negative effects. Better instructions (ScaleVLN-rewrite) and decision-rich routes each add gains at matched data scale.
method: Panoramic baseline: replaces current and history perspective images with RGB ERPs, with the agent heading centered, using Qwen3.5-4B and the same actions (forward 25 cm, left/right 15°, stop).
Long action-sequence supervision: the model predicts the next H=18 expert actions autoregressively (padded with stop) with a teacher-forced NLL loss.

Confidence-guided execution (CGE): per-action uncertainty u=-log q(a_hat) from logits normalized over the four actions; executes the longest prefix whose cumulative uncertainty is at most B=1.2, with at least E_min=4 actions, then reobserves.
Decision-centric data: 98K trajectories over 800 HM3D scenes with frequent branching points, built from navmesh areas, filtered for rendering quality and duplicates, and verified by expert replay.

Instruction generation and verification: Qwen3.8-27B writes travel/branching/arrival segment descriptions from route videos and 8-view compass images, then checks motion consistency, choice grounding and stop grounding, keeping only samples that pass all three.
State sampling: a stride-6 grid plus extra states at sustained-turn onsets and near termination.

Geometry-aware fusion: frozen PanoVGGT features are resampled in ERP coordinates, grouped 2x2 to match the current tokens, projected by a trainable MLP and added residually (alpha=0.2) with no extra tokens; current frame gets N_c tokens and history frames fewer (N_h<N_c).

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-4B (fine-tuned) + frozen PanoVGGT geometry encoder + trainable MLP projector
setting.training_data: R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrations, DAgger data, and the authors' 98K-trajectory decision-centric HM3D dataset (800 scenes); the † variant uses only R2R-CE/RxR-CE plus DAgger
setting.observation: RGB-only equirectangular panoramas (current plus up to 10 history frames from the last 100 observations), no depth or odometry
setting.action_space: low-level forward 25 cm / turn left or right 15° / stop, predicting 18 actions per call
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes for evaluation, HM3D for training data)

numbers_note: Prediction horizon and training-data scale ablations are given only as figures. Real-world SR/NE are in a figure; Table 2 reports only efficiency metrics.
results: With a 4B backbone and RGB-only panoramas, PanoVLN reaches SR 77.3 on R2R-CE and 78.0 on RxR-CE val-unseen, 11.9 and 8.7 points above the previous best (CorrectNav SR 65.1 / 69.3 in Table 1, among the strongest baselines). On a Unitree Go2 it navigates faster (86.4 s vs 117.8 s for StreamVLN) with fewer pauses and policy calls.
limitations: Long-horizon prediction with CGE needs tuned hyperparameters (H, B, E_min), and per-call latency (1.08 s) is higher than StreamVLN's (0.58 s).
Real-world evaluation is small (20 routes per setting, 5 methods) and needs a 360° camera and a remote GPU.
Gains depend on a large synthetic dataset built with a strong VLM plus DAgger, so the contribution of each source is partly entangled.
